Senior Colonel Zhang Xiaogang, Spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defense (MND), answered media queries on April 30.

More information is provided below:

Question: It is reported that the Japan Self-Defense Forces participates in this year's US-Philippines Exercise Balikatan, marking the first time for Japanese combat forces to set foot in the Philippines since the end of World War II. Philippine WWII victim associations and civil society groups have come out in opposition and protest. What is your comment on this?

Zhang Xiaogang: Like many of you, I understand the feelings of the Philippine people concerning this year's Balikatan military exercise. During World War II, Japanese aggressors committed numerous crimes in the Philippines, including the Manila Massacre and the forced recruitment of "comfort women". In addition, there was the Bataan Death March, which, together with the Nanjing Massacre and the Burma-Thailand Death Railway, are known as the three major war atrocities in the Far East. In April 1942, the Japanese military captured Bataan Peninsula. Around 78,000 American and Philippine troops that had already surrendered, were systematically abused. They were forced to march 120 kilometers on foot to Camp O'Donnell, and 15,000 died miserably. To this day, the perpetrators of those atrocities have not shown genuine remorse for their crimes. How could this historical trauma be healed? Relevant countries should not forget the lessons learned from the painful history, listen to the voice of the people, stop stoking division and confrontation, and jointly thwart Japan's "neomilitarism", so as to maintain peace and tranquility in the Asia-Pacific.

“Little Sparta” as General James Mattis calls the U.A.E., is front and center on @WSJ this AM, w/ story that begins:

“The United Arab Emirates’ decision to withdraw from OPEC did more than deliver a shock to the cartel that has long ruled the global oil market. It also rang the opening bell for the new geopolitical order that the war with Iran is ushering in across the Middle East.

The new alignment is redrawing political fault lines between the Arab world and Israel that defined the region for decades. Instead, the U.A.E.—the financial nerve center of the Gulf and a potent military power—is strengthening security cooperation with Israel as both states work to change the region’s strategic balance through force of arms if necessary.

Israel recently sent its Iron Dome missile-defense technology and troops to operate it to the Gulf state, people familiar with the matter said, something that would be unthinkable elsewhere in the Arab world.

The war has given the U.A.E., a small and fantastically wealthy federation of monarchies, an opportunity to emerge from the shadow of its larger neighbor Saudi Arabia and make a statement about its aspirations for regional power.

The U.A.E. pointedly signaled its new priorities by announcing its exit from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, the one body the Arab world has ever been able to use to throw around its collective clout, at the exact moment Gulf leaders were meeting in Saudi Arabia in an attempted show of unity. 

The decision was timed to deliver a shock and to make a statement that the U.A.E.’s national interest comes first, Emirati officials familiar with the decision said. The U.A.E. is also rethinking its ties to organizations including the Arab League and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, according to officials familiar with the discussions. Asked for comment, a U.A.E. official said no further withdrawals are planned for now.”

The “Quad” in the Pacific is the U.S., Japan, Australia and Indian (and “Quad-adjacent countries like Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan and possibly Vietnam). 

The “Quad” in the ME ought to be U.S., Israel, U.A.E. and Saudi Arabia. (Again, there are some Quad-adjacent countries there like Bahrain and Kuwait.) The new “Iran Breakdown” from @mdubowitz and SA scholar @BernardHaykel focuses on The Kingdom and the complex strategies of MBS (link in replies). The Crown Prince may have to act much more quickly than he had planned. 

Lord Palmerston said it best long ago: “Therefore I say that it is a narrow policy to suppose that this country or that is to be marked out as the eternal ally or the perpetual enemy of England. We have no eternal allies, and we have no perpetual enemies. Our interests are eternal and perpetual, and those interests it is our duty to follow.”

x402 The Age of The Machine

The machines are getting wallets. I dug into what happened this week and the picture that emerged is worth your time.

Meta launched stablecoin payouts for creators today. USDC. On Solana and Polygon. Via Stripe. Three billion users. Colombia and Philippines first, then one hundred and sixty countries by year end.

Google built AP2, their AI agent payment protocol. Coinbase built x402. OpenAI and Stripe built ACP. Franklin Templeton built x402 directly on the XRP Ledger. Their agents pay in XRP.

Here is what I connected when I put those side by side.

Every one of these companies is building on a different chain.

Meta is on Solana and Polygon. Google AP2 is multi-chain. Coinbase x402 runs on Base. OpenAI routes through Stripe fiat rails. Franklin Templeton is on XRPL. Stripe settles across Ethereum, Solana, and Polygon.

They cannot natively talk to each other.

A Meta agent paying a Google agent has to cross chains. 

A Stripe settlement hitting an XRPL vault has to bridge. 

An OpenAI agent paying a Franklin Templeton agent needs something in the middle that both sides trust, that neither side controls, and that has no issuer who can pick up the phone and freeze the transaction.

Galaxy Research estimates three to five trillion dollars in agentic commerce by 2030. That is machine paying machine, across every blockchain, across every border, around the clock.

Every one of those cross-chain settlements needs a neutral bridge.

Now add the other layer.

Every stablecoin in this stack has a kill switch. USDC — Circle can freeze it.

Tether froze 340 million dollars with one instruction in April 2026. Stripe, Meta, and Google are all building on assets with issuers who respond to instructions. When a government decides certain agents cannot transact, the call goes to the issuer. 

The transaction stops.

XRP has no issuer. 
No freeze function. 
No kill switch at base protocol level. 

It settles in three to five seconds. 
It bridges every chain in this stack without picking a side.

Franklin Templeton did not put x402 on XRPL by accident. They built the agentic payment infrastructure for the new economy on the one rail without an off switch.

The more stablecoins that exist, the more chains that launch, the more AI agents that spin up, the more bridges that get needed between all of them.

XRP is the bridge.

We connected the dots. 🛡️
